item.title: Men’s Wearhouse Owner Tailored Brands Files Publicly for US IPO
item.description: Menswear company Tailored Brands Inc. filed publicly for an initial public offering, marking the latest step in its return to public markets.

item.title: Exxon Supports SEC Proposal to End Mandatory Quarterly Reports
item.description: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. supports a US Securities and Exchange Commission proposal to replace quarterly financial reporting with semiannual disclosures, bucking the trend among most respondents the regulator’s request for comments.

item.title: Aston Martin Lender Group Led by Arini, BlackRock, Sculptor
item.description: Aston Martin creditors led by Arini Capital Management, BlackRock Inc. and Sculptor Capital have joined forces in an effort to stop the distressed British luxury carmaker from pursuing any debt deal they fear could erode their standing.

item.title: Nasdaq Says SK Hynix Bonanza Opens Path to More Foreign Listings
item.description: Nasdaq Inc. President Nelson Griggs said SK Hynix Inc.’s blockbuster listing is spurring other international companies to consider the US for either initial public offerings or the sales of American depositary receipts.

item.title: SK Hynix CEO Expects Memory Crunch to Last Into Next Decade
item.description: The memory-chip shortages that are roiling the computer, car and device markets will probably persist beyond 2030, according to SK Hynix Inc. Chief Executive Officer Kwak Noh-Jung.

item.title: BHP Explores Sale of Chilean Desalination Plant, Power Lines
item.description: BHP Group is exploring the sale of a desalination plant in Chile, along with its electricity transmission assets, extending a strategy of monetizing infrastructure as the world’s biggest miner concentrates capital on its core copper business, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US Eases Export Curbs on UAE, Opening Door for AI Chip Sales
item.description: The Trump administration plans to ease export restrictions on the United Arab Emirates, clearing the way for the Gulf state to buy a wide range of advanced technologies including commercial satellites and semiconductors used for artificial intelligence.

item.title: Gasoline Prices Fuel Fresh Acceleration in Russian Inflation
item.description: Russia’s inflation accelerated sharply in June after Ukrainian strikes on the country’s oil refineries triggered gasoline shortages and sent fuel prices higher.

item.title: Miner ERG Weighs Breakup to Split Assets Between Its Owners
item.description: The owners of Eurasian Resources Group are considering splitting the mining group into two businesses, in an overhaul that would separate its Kazakh and international operations.

item.title: Fed Vows to Deliver Price Stability in Monetary Policy Report
item.description: Federal Reserve policymakers again vowed to deliver price stability even as inflation remains well above the central bank’s 2% target, making the pledge in the central bank’s semiannual Monetary Policy Report to Congress that was released Friday in Washington.

item.title: The Stock Market and a “Phenomena of our Lifetimes”
item.description: Something big has changed in the makeup of the US economy.

item.title: Delayed Xbox Layoffs Leave Employees Scared And Nervous
item.description: Xbox cut 1,600 jobs this week and plans to cut another 1,600 over the next 12 months, leaving remaining staff on tenterhooks

item.title: SK Chairman Promises ‘Much, Much Bigger’ US Investment Plan
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, fresh off a landmark US stock offering for the conglomerate’s memory-chip business, said he has an ambitious plan to invest more money in America.

item.title: SK Chairman Says Company May Offer ‘Memory as a Service’
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. is considering new ways of selling access to its memory chips, including a concept called “memory as a service,” suggesting customers could rent usage from the South Korean company rather than purchasing the actual semiconductors.

item.title: SK Hynix Open to Issuing More US Shares, SK Group Chairman Says
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. is open to issuing more US shares should returns prove strong and the company’s stock price remains stable, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said.

item.title: Turkey Central Bank Sees July Inflation as Key for Rate Outlook
item.description: Turkey’s central bank wants to see more evidence of slowing inflation and clarity on the Iran conflict before resuming monetary easing, Governor Fatih Karahan has told investors.

item.title: Sports Bet Pays Off as Omers Reaps Nearly 60% Gain on MLSE
item.description: Ontario’s pension fund for government workers generated a return of close to 60% in less than three years on an bet tied to Toronto’s major league sports teams, vindicating an investment that was initially viewed as pricey.

item.title: Europeans Are Changing Saving Habits to Invest More, ING Says
item.description: Europeans are showing a durable shift in savings habits toward products such as investment funds that might one day help support greater spending, ING economists said.

item.title: Morgan Stanley Sees Pressure Rising on Chipmakers’ Pricing Power
item.description: Morgan Stanley’s Lisa Shalett urged investors to be cautious on chipmakers as evidence mounts that their pricing power is limited, suggesting that the stocks may have rallied too far on optimism around artificial-intelligence spending.

item.title: La dette cachée freine le développement du Sénégal: Next Africa
item.description: Les grands projets d’infrastructure devaient incarner la transformation du Sénégal en l’une des économies les plus dynamiques d’Afrique de l’Ouest.

item.title: SK Hynix Indicated to Climb 21% After $26.5 Billion ADR Offering
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s American depositary receipts are indicated to open 21% above their offering price, after the South Korean memory chipmaker raised $26.5 billion in the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company.

item.title: Prediction Market Bets Surge on World Cup Mania
item.description: Rabid interest in the World Cup has helped to drive more than $3 billion of wagers on a prediction market backed by Robinhood Markets Inc. and Susquehanna International Group, which launched just a few months ago.

item.title: Retail Traders Chase Shiny Objects But Refuse to Bet on S&P 500
item.description: Retail traders, some of the staunchest supporters of the stock market this decade, are showing signs of waning conviction.

item.title: AlphaQuest Founder Lost Control at Quant Fund, Investor Alleges
item.description: AlphaQuest founder Nigol Koulajian admitted losing control of trading at his $2 billion quantitative hedge fund before announcing plans to shut it down, an institutional investor claimed in a lawsuit.

item.title: Macro Hedge Fund Deem Raised $1 Billion From Abu Dhabi’s ADIC
item.description: Asfandyar Nadeem’s hedge fund has received about $1 billion in new capital from an Abu Dhabi investor, amid a surge in appetite for macro strategies and as the Gulf city accelerates its drive to become a key backer of the industry.

item.title: Raytheon, Rheinmetall Anchor AI Training Effort for UK Army
item.description: The UK Ministry of Defense awarded a £2 billion ($2.7 billion) contract for AI-based military training to a Raytheon-led consortium that includes European defense prime Rheinmetall AG.

item.title: Czech Price Pressures Warrant Increased Caution for Central Bank
item.description: The Czech central bank said monetary policy caution remains warranted, with the headline inflation rate likely to return to or “slightly above” the 2% target this year following a recent drop.

item.title: Canada Adds 18,200 Jobs in June as Young Workers Catch a Break
item.description: Employment in Canada rose 18,200 in June and the unemployment rate fell to 6.5% as the country’s labor market shows some signs of tightening.

item.title: Brazil Inflation Surprise Bolsters Case for More Rate Cuts
item.description: Brazil’s annual inflation unexpectedly slowed in June, offering some relief to policymakers after the central bank delivered its third consecutive interest-rate cut even as price growth remained above target.

item.title: Shein Gets Approval From Chinese Regulator for Hong Kong IPO
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. got approval from the Chinese regulator to move ahead with its planned initial public offering in Hong Kong, capping a yearslong effort by the fast-fashion giant to go public.
